issues.why_it_applies_here: The stated use case requires each accepted bank\u2192ID match to be defensible to an investment committee before a position is sized; the killing risk is a confident wrong match. An optimal-transport assignment with conformal calibration cannot be traced by hand \u2014 the PM cannot see why ID 4471 was called ING rather than ABN. The plan owes a simple corroborating check the audience can verify itself and does not provide one.
issues.what_breaks: Every accepted match feeds a position, but the acceptance is a black box; the PM cannot underwrite the one thing that kills the desk.
issues.fix: For each accepted match, produce a one-page human-readable dossier: the 2-3 features that dominated the score (e.g. Kindergeld-digit signature, NUTS-3 branch overlap, salary payday concentration), shown as raw distributions against the anchor, plus the runner-up candidate and why it lost. The optimal-transport layer can run underneath, but a person must be able to confirm the top matches by eye.

issues.summary: The joint-assignment global optimizer is complexity ahead of demonstrated need; a simple per-ID scoring pass should be shown to fail before the transport layer is built.
issues.why_it_applies_here: In concentrated markets (NL, SE) with a handful of large banks, most IDs will separate on n_share and geography alone \u2014 the injective-map hypothesis says exactly this. The min-cost-flow-with-capacities apparatus only earns its place in fragmented markets (350 Sparkassen) where the plan itself predicts identification fails. So the heavy machinery is being built precisely where the answer is 'not identifiable.'
issues.what_breaks: Engineer and data-team weeks go into Sinkhorn/Gibbs entropy matching before anyone has shown a naive greedy assignment is insufficient in the markets that matter.
issues.fix: Run the Netherlands pilot with plain per-ID likelihood scoring and greedy assignment first. Add the joint optimizer only if greedy produces mutually inconsistent assignments at the target precision.

issues.summary: Validation-label supply (25-60 per country, floor 15) is thin, and precision at the \u226595% target is being certified on very few positives.
issues.why_it_applies_here: To claim \u226595% precision you need enough validated true matches that a handful of errors moves the estimate materially; with 25-60 labels per country and leave-one-institution-out refitting, the precision confidence interval will be wide. The plan is honest that below 15 it is unvalidatable, but 25-60 still cannot distinguish 95% from 85% precision reliably.
issues.what_breaks: A country could pass the 40%/95% gate on a precision estimate that is really a small-sample fluke, and the desk sizes on it.
issues.fix: Report precision with its Clopper-Pearson interval and require the lower bound (not point estimate) to clear 95%; expand consented-survey seeding where the label count is marginal, or restrict deployment to institutions with direct provider-revealed seeds.

issues.summary: The largest concrete deliverable is a boolean identifiability map, but the firm's actual downstream need \u2014 which specific tickers can be underwritten \u2014 is only implicit.
issues.why_it_applies_here: This is a capability build and correctly scoped as one; success is measurement, not a P&L. But the firm names four behaviors (deposit flows, salary capture, acquisition, attrition) it wants to underwrite. The plan should state which of those signals survive the match uncertainty \u2014 a 92%-precision match may be fine for a directional attrition read but unsafe for a levered pairs trade.
issues.what_breaks: A binary 'identifiable' verdict hands the desk matches without telling them which use each match is good enough for.
issues.fix: Deliver, per accepted match, the confidence and the customer-count support alongside a note on which of the four underwriting signals that support can carry, so the PM sizes accordingly.

response.overall: This is a well-constructed capability build with the right error posture \u2014 Type-I-dominant, abstain-heavy, kill criterion and negative controls front-loaded, register separation to prevent anchor leakage, and genuine engagement with what would make it wrong. The binding defect is that the matching method is too sophisticated for the PM who must defend each match; optimal transport and conformal calibration cannot answer 'what would have to be true for this to be wrong' unless each accepted match ships with a hand-checkable dossier. Start with the Netherlands using plain per-ID scoring, and build the transport layer only if the simple version demonstrably fails.

issue_buckets.why: Not in gold. It is anchored in this firm's stated constraint (must be defensible to a PM asking what would have to be true for it to be wrong) and names the specific machinery (min-cost flow, Sinkhorn marginals, Venn-Abers) rather than reciting a generic 'black box' worry, so a desk would take it seriously. Discounted somewhat because the plan does supply hand-checkable corroboration the evaluator claims is absent: acceptance requires max p >= 0.80, margin >= 0.25, and >= 3 comparators favouring, plus typed abstain reasons and near-tie candidate sets \u2014 which is close to the 'simple corroborating check' being asked for. Legitimate but partly overstated.

Not the gold objection (gold's disproportionality points at manufactured labels, anchor maintenance, and the GDPR gate, not the assignment layer). The point is nonetheless earned on this plan's own internal logic: the plan predicts identification succeeds where markets are concentrated (few candidates, separable on n_share/geo) and fails where they are fragmented (350 Sparkassen), so the capacitated transport plus Sinkhorn/Gibbs entropy-matching apparatus is heaviest exactly where the plan expects a null. That is a specific, checkable sequencing critique, not a canonical complexity complaint. Marked uncertain because it partially rhymes with the gold's 'everything else is disproportionate' framing.

Overlaps the gold's topic (validation labels) but makes a different objection: power rather than feasibility. It is quantitatively grounded in the plan's own numbers \u2014 certifying >= 95% precision off 25-60 labels per country under leave-one-institution-out refitting, against a 40% deposit-volume gate \u2014 so it is not a recited small-sample platitude; it bites on this specific acceptance criterion. Uncertain because a desk might treat it as the same conversation as the gold's label critique.

Not in gold, and legitimate here: the firm named four specific behaviours to underwrite (deposit flows, salary capture, acquisition, attrition), while the plan's deliverable is a per-country boolean identifiability verdict at a single 95% precision bar. Asking which signals survive a 92%-precision match \u2014 directional attrition read versus a levered pairs trade \u2014 is specific to this mandate and this precision target, not a generic 'link to P&L' complaint, and the evaluator correctly concedes the capability-build framing is right. Uncertain only because the gold implicitly credits the plan for narrowing to a ticker, which sits adjacent to this point.

response.plan_implied_asker: single-name event-driven catalyst desk reading a specific corporate structuring event
response.what_would_falsify: A signing-document condition met on schedule (H0-a); a subsidiary/keepwell/ECL substitution (observation wrong); withdrawals across unrelated vehicles (treasury policy); deconsolidation entry with VIE footnote change and CFO commentary (H0-b); no independent second-source qualification within twelve months and no available advanced packaging (H1 lacks mechanism); a take-or-pay/volume floor/RVG replacing the guarantee (risk transfer falsified).

issues.summary: The comparable-release coding exercise (40-60 cases across three strata) is a generalizable base-rate study bolted onto a single-name call and largely duplicates work the document read already does.
issues.why_it_applies_here: The desk has two analysts, no dataset-building capacity, and the question is whether THIS situation is mispriced now. The signing documents themselves state whether the release was a scheduled condition (H0-a) — reading the Guaranty Release Date and completion triggers resolves the dominant benign explanation directly, without coding 50 unrelated project-finance deals. The base-rate prior is useful as a sanity anchor but the plan front-loads a weeks-long coding project the staff cannot cheaply run.
issues.what_breaks: Methodology step consumes the scarce analyst weeks before the catalyst window closes; a weeks-to-months horizon can pass while comparables are being coded.
issues.fix: Read the original documents first — if the release is a scheduled condition met on terms, stop. Only if the trigger is negotiated/unexplained does the comparable set add value, and then cap it at a handful of genuine semiconductor-capacity JV analogs, not 50 cross-strata deals.

issues.summary: The ~25x likelihood-ratio hurdle against a 20:1-30:1 prior is a manufactured quantitative bar the evidence sources cannot actually feed.
issues.why_it_applies_here: The H1 evidence is qualitative and sparse — hiring reqs, MPW activity, teardowns, customs data on one situation. There is no way to compute a calibrated 25x likelihood ratio from these; the number invents precision the design cannot deliver and risks either false rigor or an impossible-to-clear gate that discards a real signal (Type II) or a rationalized clearing of it (Type I).
issues.what_breaks: The Bayesian framing implies a numeric verdict that the actual evidence stream cannot support, letting the analyst assign convenient LRs to reach a predetermined conclusion.
issues.fix: Keep the directional prior (benign causes dominate, demand strong contemporaneous second-source evidence) but drop the pseudo-numeric LR. State the qualitative pattern that would count as confirmation and the pattern that would count as kill — the falsifier list already does this well.

issues.summary: H3 (souring project) is flagged as externally identical to H1 but the separation rests entirely on demand-side evidence that may not be observable in the window.
issues.why_it_applies_here: The plan correctly notes H3 and H1 have opposite trade implications and identical financing footprints. But the demand-side signals it relies on to separate them (node slip, insourcing, demand shortfall) are exactly the things a hyperscaler and foundry disclose last and least. If separation fails, the trade direction is undetermined.
issues.what_breaks: Even a clean H1-vs-H0 result leaves the position exposed to being long the wrong sign if the release actually reflects a souring project.
issues.fix: Make H1/H3 separation a pre-committed gate: if demand-side evidence cannot distinguish them within the catalyst window, the situation is not tradeable and the position should not be put on regardless of how strong the strategic read looks.

response.overall: A genuinely strong single-name plan that fits the desk: document-first, catalyst-horizoned, with real pre-registered falsifiers and explicit engagement with the benign alternatives and the opposite-sign H3 case. The main defects are self-imposed over-engineering — a 50-case comparable-coding study and a pseudo-numeric likelihood-ratio hurdle that neither the staff nor the evidence can support — which should be trimmed in favor of reading the signing documents first, since a scheduled-condition release kills the thesis in days. Watch that H1 and H3 remain separable within the window; if not, the situation is not tradeable.

issue_buckets.why: Matches gold blocking#3 (dataset build beyond desk capacity) and overlaps the subject of blocking#1, framed as unnecessary complexity/duplication of the document read.

Matches gold blocking#2: the 20:1-30:1 prior and 25x LR hurdle are invented precision that reads as discipline; evaluator adds the specific point that the qualitative evidence stream cannot feed a calibrated LR.

Not in gold. Legitimate and specific to this situation: the plan concedes H3 is externally identical to H1 and defers to demand-side evidence, but node slip / insourcing / demand shortfall are precisely what a hyperscaler and a foundry disclose last, so the trade sign may stay undetermined even after H0 is cleared. Earned against this plan's own pitfall list rather than recited boilerplate.

response.plan_implied_asker: single-name event-driven credit/equity desk trading a catalyst over weeks-to-months
response.what_would_falsify: Release language verbatim as-signed with the pre-agreed test (COD/DSCR) met; no consent solicitation or consent fee; VIE exposure-to-loss dropping below released notional; capacity volumes flat or rising; no second-source qualification predating the change. Any two of these and H1 is rejected.

issues.summary: The near-dispositive H3 test relies on back-solving redacted contract quantities and on a QoQ delta in the hyperscaler's VIE maximum-exposure-to-loss disclosure that may not be granular or timely enough to attribute to this SPV.
issues.why_it_applies_here: The plan itself names the exposure-to-loss delta as 'best H3 test' but hyperscalers disclose VIE max-exposure in aggregate, not per-SPV; a single new SPV can be swamped by other VIEs and the disclosure lags by a quarter. Back-solving redactions under 601(b)(10)(iv) is explicitly flagged as necessary because the key numbers are hidden.
issues.what_breaks: The H3 kill/confirm step may return an unmeasurable or ambiguous number, leaving the H1-vs-H3 distinction unresolved right where the plan says it is decided.
issues.fix: State a fallback when the aggregate delta is uninformative: rely on the as-signed guarantee article language and reserve/LC face directly, and mark H3 'indeterminate' rather than forcing a read from a noisy aggregate.

issues.summary: Qualification-timing evidence (second source predating the change) is inferred from noisy public tells — job postings, conference papers, bill-of-lading, EDA/IP disclosures — none of which timestamp a decision cleanly.
issues.why_it_applies_here: The H1 story hinges on qualification preceding the guarantor removal by 18-36 months, but the listed corroborants are lagging and ambiguous: a PDK license or IEDM paper signals engagement, not committed second-sourcing on this design family, and dates are fuzzy.
issues.what_breaks: 'No qualification predating the change' is one of the named killers; if the timing evidence is inherently soft, that killer can be neither cleanly triggered nor cleanly cleared, weakening the falsification test.
issues.fix: Require at least one hard, dated corroborant (a mask-set/tape-out order, a dated NRE payment, a specific packaging requal booking) before treating pre-dating qualification as established; treat soft tells as supporting-only.

issues.summary: The document-heavy front end is a large fixed workload before the cheapest disconfirming check.
issues.why_it_applies_here: The plan does place 'check the price reaction first' in pitfalls and orders H2/H3 before H1, but the 300-page as-signed document pull and redaction back-solve is heavy and could be gated behind a first-pass read of whether the release simply matches vintage-standard COD/DSCR language.
issues.what_breaks: Analyst time is the binding constraint on a two-analyst desk; if the release is boilerplate springing off a met test (H2), most of the supply-agreement and channel work is wasted.
issues.fix: Explicitly front the single check that most cheaply kills the thesis: does the release language match the pre-agreed COD/DSCR test in the as-signed docs and was that test met? If yes, stop before the supply-agreement and channel program.

response.overall: A well-constructed single-name event-driven plan that fits the desk exactly: legal-document primary work, expert channel, fast kill criteria, cheapest-disconfirmation-first ordering, an explicit falsifier, a base-rate cross-check, and sizing anchored to observable release spread rather than an invented alpha figure. It correctly predicts the target (is this situation mispriced now) and matches the Type-I-dominant, IC-traceable posture of a concentrated catalyst book. The real weaknesses are measurement, not design — the two near-dispositive tests (VIE exposure-to-loss delta and qualification-timing) rest on disclosures that may be too aggregated or too soft to trigger the stated killers cleanly, so the plan should name fallbacks and demand at least one hard dated corroborant before committing capital.

issue_buckets.why: Not in gold, but earned and plan-specific: it attacks the very disclosure the plan nominates as its 'best H3 test', noting VIE maximum-exposure-to-loss is reported in aggregate and lagged, so a single new SPV's delta may be unattributable — and pairs that with the acknowledged 601(b)(10)(iv) redactions. A desk would take this seriously; it is not a recited canonical objection.

Not in gold, but a legitimate and specific critique: the plan makes 'no qualification predating the change' a named killer while sourcing timing from PDK licensing, conference papers, job postings and trade data, which signal engagement rather than committed second-sourcing and carry fuzzy dates. It bites on this plan's own falsification rule rather than being generic.

The reviewer explicitly ruled this out (anti_objection#2): the volume of reading B requires is not a negative because an AI reader handles the volume, and the '300 pages' framing is aimed at the wrong thing. This issue makes precisely that objection — heavy document pull, analyst time as the binding constraint on a two-analyst desk, gate the reading behind a lighter first pass — which is the concern the reviewer considered and dismissed in writing.

response.plan_implied_asker: a large systematic equity firm with production ML, tick data and a replicating research committee, days-to-weeks horizon
response.what_would_falsify: Null pre-registered: peer-relative tone residual adds no risk-adjusted return beyond SUE, announcement return, momentum and style factors; net alpha below 30bp break-even is declared a paper result; a clean null is treated as a real output.

issues.summary: The kill test — does any tone measure survive costs and orthogonalization — sits at the very end behind a full custom NLP model build.
issues.why_it_applies_here: The plan front-loads ~1.5-2B-token domain-adaptive MLM pretraining, a 6k-sentence gold annotation effort and 150k silver labels before ever checking whether a cheap tone proxy (Loughran-McDonald, off-the-shelf FinBERT) produces a residual signal that survives the FF5+MOM/SUE controls and 30bp break-even. LM and FinBERT are named only as benchmarks-to-beat, not as a first-pass gate.
issues.what_breaks: Weeks of GPU pretraining and annotation are sunk before the premise — that peer-relative call tone carries priced-in-days-to-weeks information beyond PEAD — is shown to hold at all. If LM tone already dies against the announcement-return control, the entire custom encoder was wasted.
issues.fix: Run the whole pipeline first with LM and stock FinBERT tone as the signal. Only if a crude tone residual shows net-of-cost promise does the DeBERTa domain-adaptation and gold-annotation build earn its place. Make this an explicit pre-committed gate.

issues.summary: No inspectable intermediate output is scheduled before the modelling commitment; human review appears only as post-hoc audits.
issues.why_it_applies_here: The plan lists a 200-call EDGAR timestamp audit and coverage-by-decile tables, but these are framed as pitfall checks rather than early gates. The distribution of the tone measure, hand-traced Q&A reconstruction on sample calls, and coverage/missingness by year are the things that would catch a broken parser or imputed-timestamp contamination — and nothing forces them before the encoder is built.
issues.what_breaks: A systematic parsing error (e.g. operator boilerplate leaking, mislabeled Q&A vs prepared sections) propagates silently into H2, which is the most novel claim, and is only discoverable after full training.
issues.fix: Move timestamp audit, Q&A-pair spot checks and coverage tables to the front as a pass/fail data-integrity gate before any label or model work.

issues.summary: Timestamp imputation for calls lacking minute-level start uses the 8-K press-release time, which can precede the call and create look-ahead in the announcement-return control.
issues.why_it_applies_here: The plan flags imputed timestamps but still uses (−1,+1) announcement return and t+1 entry keyed off call time. For calls where the 8-K timestamp is the release not the call, the (−1,+1) window and the tone-availability assumption misalign — tone is not actually knowable at the entry point claimed.
issues.what_breaks: Portfolio entry at t+1 close assumes tone was observable; if the true call time is later than the imputed 8-K time, the signal is partly forward-looking and inflates alpha.
issues.fix: Exclude imputed-timestamp calls from the headline specification (keep as a robustness cut), or enforce entry strictly after a conservatively latest possible call time. The 200-call audit should quantify the imputation error distribution before deciding.

response.overall: Methodologically this is among the more disciplined systematic plans one could review: pre-registered primary spec, held-out 2023-2024 touched once, explicit break-even and capacity, negative controls, placebo, a real pre-committed null, and appropriate Type-II-leaning posture for a diversified quant book. The sophisticated NLP is corroborated by LM/FinBERT benchmarks and the committee can re-run it. The one real defect is sequencing and cost: the cheap tone proxies are demoted to benchmarks when they should be the first-pass kill test, so a large annotation-and-pretraining spend is committed before the premise is shown to survive PEAD controls and transaction costs. Reorder to gate on the crude version first and the plan is sound.

issue_buckets.why: Same concern as blocking#2: the expensive custom encoder is built before establishing that a cheap tone measure (LM/FinBERT) produces a signal surviving controls and costs; LM/FinBERT used as benchmarks rather than a gate.

Not in gold. The specific point — that parser/Q&A-section reconstruction and tone-distribution inspection should be a gate before the encoder build, since H2 (Q&A vs prepared remarks) depends entirely on correct section and speaker labelling — is a legitimate desk concern and is tied to concrete artifacts in this plan. Uncertain because the plan does already schedule a 200-call EDGAR audit, coverage-by-size-decile/year tables and section markers from the vendor, so the objection is partly about framing/sequencing rather than a missing check.

Largely restates a pitfall the plan already names and mitigates ('timestamps recording publication not call time; audit 200 calls against EDGAR 8-Ks', imputed flag, pre-open/intraday/post-close classification) without showing the mitigation is insufficient. The look-ahead mechanics also do not bite as claimed: entry is t+1 close with a t+2 conservative variant, and the 8-K release generally precedes the call on the same or prior day, so the imputed time errs early, leaving the entry point after the call; and the (-1,+1) return is a control window, so misalignment is measurement error, not forward-looking signal. Flagged uncertain because minute-level alignment for the aggressive same-day-close bound is a real residual concern.

response.plan_implied_asker: a large systematic quant firm with tick data, production ML, and a replicating research committee
response.what_would_falsify: Tone t below 2.5 (2.9 Bonferroni), net spread under 3% annualised or IR under 0.4, wrong sign in more than 3 of 10 years, or spread concentrated in the bottom size quintile; plus placebo over [-63,-3] showing an incremental coefficient and vendor rank correlation above 0.7 indicating commodity duplication.

issues.summary: Vendor availability is used as the crowding proxy but the plan never diffs the final signal against what the vendor scores would already have captured beyond the one-month rank-correlation trial.
issues.why_it_applies_here: Edge here is whether the in-house tone signal is incremental to what is already sold and in books. The 0.7 rank-correlation trial checks duplication of construction, but two signals can correlate below 0.7 and still both be arbitraged. The plan infers crowding from seat cost and client count, which is a reasonable proxy, but does not test whether the net spread survives after orthogonalizing to the vendor score rather than merely using it as a control.
issues.what_breaks: Day 10 spread and Day 11-14 scope decision could greenlight a signal that is a slightly-decorrelated repackaging of a widely-licensed score, failing on capacity/crowding in production.
issues.fix: Add an explicit step regressing the in-house signal's returns on the licensed vendor score's returns and require the residual to retain a material fraction of the net spread before scope-out.

issues.summary: The 2004-2010 replication requiring t near 3 uses a period with materially different transcript coverage and market microstructure than the 2015+ primary sample.
issues.why_it_applies_here: Capital IQ / WRDS transcript coverage and timestamp reliability are thinner and less point-in-time in 2004-2010 than post-2015; the same LM within-firm-change construction may behave differently because the peer universe and coverage bias shift. Requiring t near 3 in a noisier, less-covered era could either falsely kill a real recent effect or falsely validate on a smaller, size-skewed early sample.
issues.what_breaks: Days 6-7 replication gate may reject or accept for reasons of data regime rather than signal decay, contaminating the decay-curve estimate that the whole prior rests on.
issues.fix: Report coverage and timestamp-quality diagnostics for 2004-2010 alongside the replication, and treat the early-period t as directional evidence for the decay curve rather than a hard second gate.

response.overall: A strong, well-sequenced plan that matches the firm and the blind-fit/OOS goal, front-loads a pre-registered kill gate, and correctly treats Type II asymmetry with judgeable thresholds and negative controls. It measures the target (peer-relative return, incremental to surprise/CAR/guidance) rather than a proxy, engages decay and crowding directly, and states real falsifiers. The two open items — proving incrementality to the licensed vendor score beyond a correlation trial, and treating the early-period replication as regime-sensitive — are secondary and do not block execution.

issue_buckets.why: Legitimate and specific to this plan: the only duplication test is a one-month rank-correlation screen at 0.7, and the vendor score is used as a control rather than orthogonalized against before computing the net spread — a real gap for a desk that judges work on crowding. Overlaps in topic with blocking#2 and asks for a similar missing test (incremental alpha vs the licensed score), but inverts the reviewer's diagnosis by endorsing the availability-implies-crowding inference, so it is not the same concern; flagged uncertain because a human may prefer to score it as matched to blocking#2.

Earned against this specific design rather than recited: the Days 6-7 gate requires t near 3 on a 2004-2010 Capital IQ/WRDS replication whose transcript coverage and publication-timestamp reliability genuinely are thinner and more size-skewed than the post-2015 primary sample, and the plan's whole one-third-of-published-coefficient prior plus decay-curve estimate rests on that comparison. A desk would take the point seriously; it is not in the reviewer's list.

response.plan_implied_asker: a systematic quant equity shop with a full factor stack and pre-registration discipline
response.what_would_falsify: First-stage pooled announcement β<20bp/100bp or t<5 kills the premise; placebo/randomization must produce vanishing coefficients; split-sample 2015-2025 tested once; stability declared only if VR>=2 and bootstrap p<0.05.

issues.summary: The analytical machinery (Bai-Perron sup-F, Kalman β path, stationary block bootstrap, 2SLS, two-stage DCF for β*) is far beyond what this fund's PM and IC can evaluate or defend.
issues.why_it_applies_here: Output must 'be defensible to a PM who will ask what would have to be true for it to be wrong.' A Kalman-filtered time-varying β and a sup-F break test are not checkable by a fundamental IC; they cannot carry a sizing decision at a 30-person L/S shop with one engineer and no production ML.
issues.what_breaks: The estimation and stability sections produce numbers no one on the receiving end can interrogate, so the result either gets rubber-stamped or ignored — neither is a decision.
issues.fix: Lead with a simple, inspectable version: monthly Fama-MacBeth β with a plot of β by regime bucket and the raw scatter of ΔCAGR vs Δln(EV/EBITDA). Keep the sophisticated machinery as an appendix corroboration, not the primary deliverable.

issues.summary: The plan is scoped as a 22-year multi-regime econometric study when the fund needs a usable position-sizing input over a 6-18 month horizon.
issues.why_it_applies_here: H1 (regime-dependent β) and H2 (efficiency/drift) answer academic questions about market structure. The fund's actual use is: when a peer-relative revision hits, does the multiple re-rate in a direction and magnitude I can trade over 6-18 months? That is H2's underreaction leg plus a single stable β estimate — most of H1's regime apparatus is not decision-relevant.
issues.what_breaks: Analyst-months are spent on Bai-Perron breaks and Kalman paths that don't change a sizing rule, delaying the one output (does re-rating drift persist and is it tradeable) that the desk can act on.
issues.fix: Demote H1 to a robustness note. Make the drift/underreaction test (H2i) the primary deliverable, since that is the only leg producing an actionable, horizon-matched signal.

issues.summary: No explicit statement of what consensus/sell-side already believes about revision-to-rerating, so the incremental edge is asserted rather than established.
issues.why_it_applies_here: Post-earnings-drift and analyst-revision momentum are among the most documented and crowded anomalies in equity markets. The plan tests whether re-rating drifts (underreaction) but never asks whether that drift is already arbitraged away in the 2015-2025 half — i.e. whether the effect is available going forward.
issues.what_breaks: If the underreaction leg is real historically but decayed post-2010 (as revision-momentum broadly has), the fund sizes into a priced effect. The split-sample tests significance but not economic availability net of crowding.
issues.fix: Add a decay/availability check: compare drift magnitude 2003-2014 vs 2015-2025 explicitly, and state where this differs from standard revision-momentum (the peer-relative, within-industry framing is the plausible variant view — make that claim explicit and test it against a plain revision-momentum benchmark).

issues.summary: Type II is the expensive error here but the gates are tuned like a concentrated Type-I setting — t>5 first stage, VR>=2 stability threshold — risking discarding a real weaker effect.
issues.why_it_applies_here: This is a diversified cross-sectional L/S signal across thousands of firm-months; a false positive is absorbed across many small peer-relative bets, a missed real effect is permanent opportunity cost. A first-stage t>5 gate is far stricter than the setting's payoff warrants and could stop the project on a genuine but modest β.
issues.what_breaks: The feasibility gate could kill a tradeable effect because it demanded near-impossible significance rather than economic magnitude relevant to a diversified book.
issues.fix: Replace the t>5 kill with an economic-magnitude gate (β large enough net of turnover costs to matter over 6-18 months) plus a consistency-across-regimes gut check; reserve high t-thresholds for the single-name overlays, not the pooled first stage.

issues.summary: TAQ/tick reverse-causality check requires intraday data the fund explicitly does not have.
issues.why_it_applies_here: Context states no tick data or execution infrastructure. The identification section relies on a 'from 2010, TAQ check: pre- vs post-activation 2-hour signed returns.' The fund cannot execute this step.
issues.what_breaks: The reverse-causality control is unbuildable in-house; either it silently gets skipped (undermining the identification claim) or requires new data licensing the plan didn't budget.
issues.fix: Drop the TAQ step and substitute a daily-resolution reverse-window check (already present via CAR(-5,-2) leakage estimate), or flag the intraday check as out-of-scope and state the resulting identification limitation.

response.overall: The research design is technically strong and largely well-suited to the question — it correctly de-circularizes the multiple, uses realized LTM denominators, front-loads a feasibility kill, and states real falsifiers. But it is written for a systematic quant shop with econometric infrastructure this fundamental fund lacks, and its sophistication (Kalman β, Bai-Perron, 2SLS) cannot be defended to the PM/IC who must act on it. Strip to the inspectable core — a simple regime-bucketed β and the underreaction drift test — loosen the over-strict Type-I gates given the diversified payoff, and make the variant-view versus crowded revision-momentum explicit before this changes any position size.

issue_buckets.why: Not in gold as a standalone item (gold#3 is about answering the wrong question, not about method opacity). The objection is earned against this specific plan: it names the actual machinery in the plan (Bai-Perron sup-F with 15% trimming, Kalman β path, VR≥2 rule, 2SLS, DCF-derived β*) and ties it to the stated firm constraint that output must be defensible to a PM asking what would have to be true for it to be wrong, at a shop with one engineer and no production ML. A desk would take this seriously.

Same concern as gold blocking#3: the project is scoped around regime stability and efficiency rather than delivering the elasticity/sizing input the seed question and the firm's 6-18 month decision horizon require.

Not in gold. Borderline canonical ('no stated edge vs. consensus') but it is specified concretely: revision momentum and PEAD are among the most documented and decayed anomalies, and the plan's split-sample test (fit 2003-2014, test 2015-2025) checks statistical significance rather than post-crowding economic availability, which is the actual gating question for H2's underreaction leg. Earned enough to escalate rather than dismiss, but the justification edges toward the generic 'is the effect already priced' recitation.

Not in gold, and it bites on specific numbers in this plan: the first-stage stop rule of β≥20bp with t>5 and the VR≥2-plus-bootstrap-p<0.05 instability rule are unusually conservative for a diversified cross-sectional peer-relative signal where a missed modest effect is the costly error. The point engages the plan's own thresholds rather than reciting a generic power complaint.

Same target as gold blocking#2 — the TAQ intraday reverse-causality check. Raised on the firm's lack of tick data, which the reviewer also names, though the evaluator misses the stronger horizon-mismatch reason and rates it only secondary.

response.plan_implied_asker: a quant-leaning fundamental fund with a strong data team, comfortable with panel econometrics
response.what_would_falsify: Placebo peer reassignment (500 draws) should collapse β1; ΔCAGR(t+1) should be insignificant as a pre-trend check; and if quintile-sort out-of-sample spread is flat the practical case fails.

issues.summary: The deliverable is a re-rating relationship among peers but the design measures whether the multiple moves with revisions, not whether that predicts future relative stock returns the fund would trade on.
issues.why_it_applies_here: Output is meant to change position sizing on named companies over 6-18mo. The estimator's DV is contemporaneous QoQ Δlog(EV/EBITDA) regressed on contemporaneous ΔCAGR. A contemporaneous elasticity tells you the market re-rates when consensus revises — which is largely mechanical and already priced. The tradeable question is whether a revision not yet fully reflected predicts subsequent relative return. The monthly t->t+1 version is buried as a 'timing' robustness check rather than being the headline.
issues.what_breaks: The main regression can be strongly significant and economically coherent yet carry zero investable edge, because it documents simultaneous adjustment, not anticipation. Sizing decisions built on it would be sizing on something already in the price.
issues.fix: Promote the predictive specification (revision at t, forward relative return over next 1-2 quarters) to the headline. Report the contemporaneous elasticity only as a sanity check on the pricing mechanism, not as the deliverable.

issues.summary: No stated edge relative to what is already priced — revision-multiple co-movement is among the most heavily mined relationships in equities.
issues.why_it_applies_here: The plan never diffs its finding against consensus or crowding. That estimate revisions drive re-ratings is textbook and traded by every quant revision/PEAD strategy. The plan's implicit edge is 'better measurement' (constant-horizon EBITDA, point-in-time Visible Alpha, EV construction with pensions/minorities), but it never establishes that this measurement improvement isolates a re-rating component that is NOT already captured by standard revision factors.
issues.what_breaks: Even a clean, significant result confirms a priced effect. Without a residualization against known revision/momentum factors, the fund cannot tell whether it has found anything incremental.
issues.fix: Add a step orthogonalizing ΔCAGR (or its predictive spread) against standard estimate-revision and price-momentum factors, and show the incremental predictive content survives. State explicitly what the market is getting wrong that this measurement captures.

issues.summary: The kill test — does anything survive out of sample and predict returns — sits at the very end behind an enormous construction and robustness apparatus.
issues.why_it_applies_here: The practical validation (out-of-sample quintile sort from 2012, spread/t-stat) is the only step that would tell the PM whether this is investable, and it is the last item. The whole point-in-time EV build, EB shrinkage, Driscoll-Kraay layering, dispersion terciles and industry interactions all precede it. A crude version — revision quintile sort on forward relative return, on the raw I/B/E/S CAGR proxy — could establish in days whether any tradeable spread exists.
issues.what_breaks: Weeks of the data team's time are committed to constructing a pristine panel before anyone has confirmed the effect predicts anything tradeable. If the cheap sort is flat, all of it was wasted.
issues.fix: Run the crude predictive quintile sort first as a gate. Only build the full point-in-time apparatus if a meaningful forward-return spread appears.

issues.summary: H1 anchors the finding to a made-up theoretical elasticity band and treats deviation from it as validation.
issues.why_it_applies_here: The '8-12%/100bp' DCF figure and the '25-50% of theoretical is coherent' rule are asserted from a two-stage/three-stage DCF with hand-picked WACC and terminal growth. This creates a self-fulfilling acceptance band: almost any β1 in a wide range will be declared 'coherent.'
issues.what_breaks: The economic validation becomes unfalsifiable — a spurious estimate landing anywhere in 25-50% of an arbitrary theoretical number gets rubber-stamped as economically sensible.
issues.fix: Drop the theoretical band as a validation gate; use it only as loose orientation. Let the placebo and out-of-sample forward-return tests carry the falsification.

issues.summary: Effort is disproportionate to a mid-size fundamental shop's ability to use and defend it.
issues.why_it_applies_here: reghdfe with 150x80 FE, two-way clustering plus Driscoll-Kraay, empirical-Bayes shrinkage, three dispersion proxies, and a full robustness grid is heavy for a fund whose output is position sizing on named companies defensible to a PM. Much of it (EB shrinkage rank stability, alternate dispersion proxies) adds researcher degrees of freedom without changing the go/no-go decision.
issues.what_breaks: The PM cannot verify the machinery, and the sheer number of specifications invites cherry-picking whichever cut looks best. The identity decomposition (β_EV=β_EBITDA+β_multiple) IS a genuinely good, checkable corroboration and should stay — but the surrounding apparatus is over-built.
issues.fix: Keep the identity decomposition and the placebo as the defensible core. Defer dispersion proxies, EB shrinkage, and half the robustness grid until the headline predictive result is established.

issues.summary: Consensus CAGR is treated as the driver, but I/B/E/S/Visible Alpha EBITDA definitions and 'consensus' are inherited premises not tested before modelling.
issues.why_it_applies_here: EBITDA definitional drift (adjusted/reported/pre-SBC) is acknowledged in pitfalls but handled by a crude |ΔCAGR|>20pp drop rule at the tail, not by verifying up front that the EBITDA the market prices matches the EBITDA in the tape. The re-rating is against whatever number investors actually use; a mismatch introduces measurement error correlated across the whole sub-industry.
issues.what_breaks: If the consensus EBITDA definition drifts systematically within an industry, the FE will not absorb it and β could reflect definitional noise rather than growth expectations.
issues.fix: Add an early diagnostic: hand-trace a sample of firm-quarters comparing the tape's EBITDA to filings and to the number in analyst notes, per key industry, before running regressions.

response.overall: The econometrics are careful and the mechanical-contamination decomposition is a genuinely good corroborating check, but the plan answers a different question than the one that pays: it measures contemporaneous re-rating (largely priced and mechanical) rather than whether revisions predict forward relative returns, and it never establishes what is incremental to standard revision/momentum factors. The single tradeable test is buried at the end behind weeks of panel construction. Reorder: run a crude predictive revision-sort as a first-week gate, residualize against known factors, and only build the pristine panel if a forward-return spread survives.

issue_buckets.why: Same core concern as blocking#1: the contemporaneous DV/regressor pairing measures mechanical simultaneous adjustment; the fix is to move to a temporally separated (predictive) specification as the headline rather than a robustness check.

Not in gold. Legitimate for a fund that must justify sizing changes: revision-driven re-rating is a heavily mined effect and the plan never residualizes against standard revision/momentum factors, so a clean β says little that is incremental. Slight overlap with [0] and arguably off-brief for a descriptive fundamental study rather than a factor build, hence flagged for escalation.

Not in gold but a sharp desk-level point about this plan specifically: the only investability test (out-of-sample within-industry quintile sort from 2012) is the last item behind a heavy point-in-time EV build, EB shrinkage, DK SEs and a large robustness grid, and a crude version on raw I/B/E/S CAGR could be run first with a three-person data team and one engineer.

Not in gold. Grounded in the plan's own text: the 8-12%/100bp two-stage figure and the '25-50% of theoretical is coherent' rule rest on hand-picked WACC/terminal growth and create a wide unfalsifiable acceptance band, which matters because the PM's test is 'what would have to be true for it to be wrong'.

Not in gold. Fits this firm's stated constraints (one engineer, no production ML, PM-defensible output): 150x80 FE, dual SE regimes, EB shrinkage with rank-stability tests and three dispersion proxies add researcher degrees of freedom without moving the go/no-go, and the critique is specific enough to name what should be kept (the identity decomposition).

Engages the plan's actual pitfall list rather than reciting generically, and 'verify the priced EBITDA matches the tape before modelling' is a fair premise-testing demand. But the plan already flags definitional drift, prefers Visible Alpha for EBITDA, flags IFRS16, and applies a screen; and the stated mechanism ('FE will not absorb it') is inconsistent with sub-industry x quarter FE, which absorbs sub-industry-common drift. Torn between engaged critique and a data-quality concern already handled — escalate.

response.plan_implied_asker: single-name event-driven desk pricing one catalyst over weeks
response.what_would_falsify: Both legs must fail for a long: if full-year consensus revision is under ~0.5%, event-window CAR is under ~1 SD and under arithmetic-implied CAR, and straddle-implied move is not elevated, the checks are unpriced; then if guidance base rate and pass-through history show raises are plausible at this quarter, the long survives. Priced-in or policy-of-holding kills it.

issues.summary: Stage one gate ordering is right but the cheapest kill — management guidance policy at this fiscal quarter — is buried in stage two.
issues.why_it_applies_here: The plan's own default is 'no' partly because management holds the full year at this point in the calendar. If the base rate of raises at this specific fiscal quarter is near zero over 12-16 quarters, the long is dead regardless of whether checks are priced. That check is a single afternoon reading transcripts and is deterministic-ish, whereas the stage-one event study is the more elaborate work.
issues.what_breaks: You may run the full consensus-revision and event-study apparatus, gate through it, and only then discover management structurally never raises here — wasted effort on the more expensive leg.
issues.fix: Pull the guidance-history raise/hold base rate for this quarter first as a five-minute triage; if the CFO never raises at Q-whatever, write the pass note before touching the event study.

issues.summary: Arithmetic-implied CAR relies on 'defensible ACV' and 'fraction landing this fiscal year' — undisclosed inputs the desk is guessing.
issues.why_it_applies_here: The gate compares observed CAR to CAR the checks 'can arithmetically deliver,' but logo count is a non-random undersized sample (the plan admits this) and ACV/ramp-fraction are not disclosed. The implied-fundamentals anchor is therefore soft, and it drives a numeric gate threshold.
issues.what_breaks: The 'CAR under arithmetic-implied' gate condition can be pushed either way by ACV assumptions, letting the analyst rationalize into or out of the trade.
issues.fix: Report the arithmetic-implied CAR as a range under conservative/base/aggressive ACV and ramp assumptions, and require the gate to hold across the range rather than at a point estimate; treat this leg as directional, consistent with how the plan already treats the checks.

issues.summary: Regression of historical earnings-day CAR on guidance revision size has very few usable data points.
issues.why_it_applies_here: 12-16 quarters, of which only a subset had meaningful guidance revisions, is a thin regression. The plan already flags the base-rate CI as wide, but then uses a regression to 'estimate reaction' as if it produces a usable coefficient.
issues.what_breaks: The scenario-weighted expected value inherits a reaction estimate that is really eyeballing 3-4 events, and could produce false precision on sizing against the straddle.
issues.fix: Replace the regression with a simple table of the historical raise/hold events and their realized earnings-day CAR; judge by eye whether above-beat raises reliably moved the stock. Keep it as a judgeable pattern, not a fitted coefficient.

response.overall: A well-constructed single-name event-driven plan that fits the desk: it leads with the priced-in question, gates hard before spending effort on the guidance leg, states a real falsifier with both legs required, and treats the checks honestly as directional and undersized. The methods are appropriate for a two-analyst fundamental desk and the explainability supports an IC narrative. Minor improvements: triage the guidance base rate before the event study since it can kill the trade cheapest, and avoid false precision in the CAR-arithmetic anchor and the thin reaction regression.

issue_buckets.why: Genuine and plan-specific: the guidance-policy base rate at this fiscal quarter is the cheap, near-deterministic kill and the plan's own default-no rests on it, yet it sits behind the expensive event-study gate. Not in gold; a desk with one PM and two analysts would take the effort-ordering point seriously.

Legitimate and tied to this plan's specific machinery: the 'CAR under arithmetic-implied CAR' gate depends on undisclosed ACV and this-fiscal-year ramp fraction, so the gate is analyst-tunable. Overlaps the spirit of the gold blocking issue (unreliable numbers driving stop-go) without making that objection, so scored as an unlisted real point.

Reads like the canonical small-sample recital but is actually earned here: the plan explicitly proposes regressing earnings-day CAR on guidance revision size off a 12-16 quarter table where only a handful of quarters had meaningful revisions, and then feeds that coefficient into straddle-relative sizing. The evaluator did the arithmetic on this plan's own data, so the objection bites.

response.plan_implied_asker: single-name event-driven desk pricing one catalyst over weeks
response.what_would_falsify: Backtest of 8 prior quarters: if positive channel commentary preceded guidance raises only 3/8 times despite 6/8 positive checks, the signal is uninformative and the plan stops. Also ~1.0x Q2 flow-through and a market-already-owns-it check.

issues.summary: The ramp/cohort least-squares fit and Monte Carlo is heavier machinery than the decision needs, and its outputs are not directly inspectable by a fundamental desk.
issues.why_it_applies_here: The gating question — does bottom-up new-logo upside clear 75bps of FY revenue — is answerable from a simple range calc (logo delta x land value x fractional in-year ramp) long before fitting R(k) by least-squares. The MC adds researcher degrees of freedom (four fitted/shocked inputs) to a two-analyst desk with no quant staff to defend it in a risk meeting.
issues.what_breaks: Methodology step: the fitted ramp and p10/50/90 can produce a false-precision number that anchors the ≥75bps gate. If the fit is overdetermined against only 12 quarters, the confidence band is illusory.
issues.fix: Run the crude bp calc first as the go/no-go screen; only build the ramp fit if the crude number lands near the 75bps threshold and the marginal precision actually changes the decision. Keep the MC as sensitivity, not as the headline output.

issues.summary: The 8-print return regression used for sizing is estimated on tiny N and treated as a mapping from estimate change to price.
issues.why_it_applies_here: Regressing 8 post-earnings returns against forward-estimate changes is 8 data points with idiosyncratic drivers each quarter; the ≥1.2x expected-vs-implied move gate rests on a slope that cannot be estimated reliably from that N.
issues.what_breaks: Position step: the ≥1.2x hurdle inherits a noisy coefficient, so the trade-selection gate is only as good as an 8-point fit that could flip on one outlier print.
issues.fix: Treat the 8 prints as a judgeable pattern (does the stock react to guide raises, and by roughly how much) rather than a fitted coefficient; state the expected move as a reasoned range anchored to realized moves, not a regression output.

issues.summary: Guidance is a management policy decision, and the plan acknowledges but does not resolve the gap between arithmetic upside and whether the CFO actually raises.
issues.why_it_applies_here: The plan's core deliverable is bp-of-revenue arithmetic, but the print catalyst depends on a discretionary CFO choice (tenure, macro caution, sandbagging) that the plan lists in pitfalls without a step that weights it. The 75bps arithmetic can be right and the guide still not move.
issues.what_breaks: The thesis-to-catalyst link: even if in-year sensitivity clears the bar, the print may not deliver, breaking the ≥1.5x median-raise gate for reasons the model does not capture.
issues.fix: Add an explicit read on management's guidance behavior (historical beat-and-raise cadence, CFO's stated posture, whether they typically hold beats as buffer) as a named gate alongside the arithmetic, not a footnote.

response.overall: A strong, well-fit single-name plan for this desk: it front-loads a genuine kill (the 6/8 vs 3/8 backtest stops the work in week one), separates the print catalyst from the ARR thesis, is adaptive, states real falsifiers, sizes off loss rather than an invented Sharpe, and matches Type-I-dominant burden of proof with tight, pre-committed gates. The main improvements are to run the crude bp screen before building the least-squares ramp and Monte Carlo, and to treat the 8-print return regression as a judgeable pattern rather than a fitted coefficient. Approve with those trims.

issue_buckets.why: Directly corresponds to gold blocking#2: the fitted ramp curve and Monte Carlo distributional output are over-engineered false precision for a single-name, single-print decision at a desk with no quant staff, and the p10/50/90 anchors the gating threshold with an illusory confidence band.

Same family of concern as blocking#2 (statistical inference from tiny N in a single-name event setting), here applied to the 8-print return regression, and it also grazes secondary#4 on the arbitrariness of the ≥1.2x gate. It is an earned point rather than a recited small-sample reflex — the plan really does propose regressing 8 observations to set a sizing hurdle — but it is close enough to gold that I treat it as matched rather than novel; flagged uncertain because a desk might score it as a distinct, unlisted hit on the position section.

Legitimate in the abstract — the arithmetic-vs-CFO-discretion gap is the crux of whether the print is the catalyst — but only weakly earned against this plan, which already tags three years of transcripts for guidance language, tabulates guided-vs-actual flow-through, gates on 'a raise at/below flow-through', and whose backtest (positive checks 6/8, raises only 3/8) is precisely a measurement of the gap. The plan's stated hypothesis is already that management won't raise, so the objection largely pushes where the plan is already pointed; kept as real_unlisted because 'no step that explicitly weights CFO discretion' is a fair desk request.

response.plan_implied_asker: a systematic quant firm with tick data, cost modelling and independent replication; horizon days-to-weeks
response.what_would_falsify: RLOIB's incremental Fama-MacBeth t<2.0 at every horizon controlling for ALLOIB/RETOIB (lot filter adds nothing); or it survives but net-of-cost long-short alpha t<3.0 (real but unharvestable).

issues.summary: The central edge question — is RLOIB incremental to the already-known subpenny/odd-lot retail signal (RETOIB) — is buried inside a full pipeline rather than run first as a cheap kill test.
issues.why_it_applies_here: RETOIB (Boehmer-Jones-Zhang-Zhang style subpenny classification) is the established, crowded retail-flow signal. The plan's entire claim to incremental value rests on RLOIB adding something over RETOIB. That residualization/rolling-window comparison could be run in days on a subsample and would answer whether the rest of the ten-year build is worth doing.
issues.what_breaks: If RLOIB is fully spanned by RETOIB the whole cost/capacity/placebo apparatus is wasted effort; the plan schedules identification alongside everything else rather than as a gate.
issues.fix: Run RLOIB-on-RETOIB residualization on 2015-2018 first as a pre-committed gate; only build the cost and capacity layers if residual RLOIB retains predictive t-stat.

issues.summary: The 't>3.0 net alpha' bar risks discarding a real but modest signal in a Type-II-dominant setting.
issues.why_it_applies_here: For a diversified quant book a missed real effect is the expensive error. A t>3.0 net-of-cost hurdle after already controlling for six factors plus in-house ALLOIB/RETOIB factors is a stiff bar; the concern is legitimate crowding here (retail-flow-fading is a well-populated trade), so a high bar is partly defensible — but the plan should state whether a t of 2.5 with good capacity would be revisited rather than binned.
issues.what_breaks: A borderline-but-tradeable diversifying sleeve could be rejected outright.
issues.fix: Pre-specify a marginal zone (e.g. 2.0<t<3.0) that triggers capacity/correlation-to-existing-book review rather than automatic rejection.

response.overall: A strong, well-sequenced plan that fits the firm exactly: it treats the round-lot retail marker as a hypothesis to validate against the known subpenny signal, front-loads a real falsifier, models costs and capacity where crowding actually kills this trade, and includes genuine placebos and negative controls. My only substantive notes are ordering — the RETOIB-spanning test is the true kill switch and should gate the expensive build — and a mild caution that the t>3.0 net bar could discard a real diversifying effect. Approve with those refinements.

issue_buckets.why: Not in gold. The substance — RLOIB's incremental value over the established subpenny retail signal — is exactly the plan's own stated falsification test, so the objection reduces to sequencing/ordering rather than a missing test, which softens it. Still, 'gate the ten-year pipeline on a cheap RETOIB-spanning check first' is a point a desk would take seriously and is tied to this plan's specific signals rather than recited generically. Borderline between real_unlisted and manufactured; escalating.

Canonical evidence-standard recital: 'high t-bar risks Type II error, would you revisit t=2.5?' would read identically against any quant plan. The justification is generic ('for a diversified quant book a missed real effect is the expensive error') and the evaluator concedes the bar is partly defensible, so no earned bite. Worse, it presumes the diversified-sleeve framing that the reviewer's blocking critique says is the wrong business for this firm entirely — arguing about 3.0 vs 2.5 net alpha on a daily long-short book is inert when the binding question is spread capture net of adverse selection inside the quoting loop.

response.plan_implied_asker: systematic firm with deep intraday microstructure data and a replicating research committee, days-to-weeks horizon
response.what_would_falsify: H0 explicitly stated: round lots uninformative once venue controlled; concrete kill thresholds at G1 lift<2.0x/LB<1.5x, G2 recall<35%, G3 signing<70%, G4 r<0.40, G5 |t|<3 — any single partition failing all-pass blocks Phase 2

issues.summary: Benchmark C (Rule 605 wholesaler reports) is the stated cheapest kill test but the gate structure requires all of G1-G5 to pass in one partition, and C's role in early termination is under-specified relative to its billing.
issues.why_it_applies_here: The plan says C is 'spreadsheet-only, run first since it alone can kill the project' but the formal gate cascade (G1-G5) is built on TAQ/RLP infrastructure. If C alone can kill, the plan should state the C-only decision rule and threshold that would stop work before any TAQ ingestion.
issues.what_breaks: Analyst may build the 36-month TAQ dataset (a quarter's work) before running the spreadsheet check that the plan itself says could kill the premise.
issues.fix: State an explicit C-only pre-screen with a numeric threshold (e.g. if wholesaler odd-lot/fractional/dollar buckets show retail has migrated off round lots below X%, stop before TAQ build).

issues.summary: G3 signing accuracy is benchmarked against RLP-flagged known-side executions, but RLP flags are the same construct feeding G1 precision — partial circularity in the validation set.
issues.why_it_applies_here: RLP-flagged executions are used both to establish precision/lift (G1) and to score signing accuracy (G3). Because RLP is near-1.0 precision but very low recall, the subset scored in G3 is a non-representative slice of retail flow, and passing G3 on it may not generalize to the round-lot population being classified.
issues.what_breaks: G3 could pass on the RLP-visible subset while signing accuracy on the broader round-lot flow (the thing actually traded) is worse, inflating confidence going into Phase 2.
issues.fix: Score signing accuracy on an independent label source (Benchmark A sub-penny) as a cross-check, and report G3 separately for RLP-visible vs. TRF-inferred flow.

issues.summary: Latent-class (Hui-Walter) estimation in G1 is sophisticated for a committee, but the plan already supplies the simple corroborating check.
issues.why_it_applies_here: Hui-Walter latent-class estimation with multiple imperfect labels is defensible here because no ground truth exists, and the plan pairs it with plain Rule 605 accounting the committee can verify by hand — this resolves the tension rather than creating one. Noting it only to confirm the corroboration is present and adequate.
issues.what_breaks: Nothing if the simple accounting agrees with the latent-class estimate; flag only if they diverge and the plan leans on the latent-class number alone.
issues.fix: Require the two G1 estimates to agree within a stated band before treating lift as established; if they diverge, default to the hand-checkable accounting figure.

response.overall: A well-constructed mechanism test that correctly refuses to bundle identification with profitability, front-loads a cheap kill (Rule 605), states an explicit H0 and pre-committed falsifiers, and matches the firm's infrastructure and Type-II-tolerant posture. The sophisticated methods are corroborated by hand-checkable simple versions, and the horizon and explainability bars fit. Minor gaps: make the Benchmark-C-only stop rule explicit so the TAQ build isn't sunk before the spreadsheet check, and remove the partial circularity of validating signing accuracy against the same RLP construct used for precision.

issue_buckets.why: Plan-specific and checkable: G1-G5 have pre-registered numeric kill thresholds while Benchmark C — the item the plan itself bills as the cheap standalone killer — has no stated decision rule or threshold, so the ordering is asserted rather than enforced against a quarter's TAQ build. Not in gold, but a desk would take the sequencing/cost point seriously.

Legitimate and earned on this plan's specifics: RLP flags do double duty as the precision/lift basis (G1) and the scoring set for signing accuracy (G3), and the plan itself concedes RLP recall is very low, so the G3 validation slice is non-representative of the round-lot population. Adjacent to gold blocking#1's label-quality theme but a distinct mechanism (circularity / false pass rather than false kill), so scored as unlisted rather than matched.

Not an objection at all — the text concedes Hui-Walter is defensible, that the plan already pairs it with hand-checkable Rule 605 accounting, that this 'resolves the tension rather than creating one', and that nothing breaks. Filed as a secondary issue while containing no criticism that bites on the plan; it also implicitly accepts the 'no ground truth exists' premise the reviewer rejects for this firm.

response.plan_implied_asker: a concentrated fundamental long-only shop deciding on one name for an IC
response.what_would_falsify: Negative on any of: negative implied gross bookings two straight quarters; channel inventory >1.5x normal; backlog/LTA definition change in a quarter that would otherwise have declined; supplier finished-goods inventory rising two quarters while backlog called record. Plus mirror-disclosure recovery <50% implies non-binding commitments.

issues.summary: The multi-episode backtest is the heaviest single work item and its usable output arrives late, yet the cheapest kill — reading this company's own agreement disclosures adversarially — could settle the question in days.
issues.why_it_applies_here: The plan's own thresholds (Tier 1/2 share, cash support, take-or-pay damages, RPO inclusion) are all readable directly from this company's 8-Ks, footnotes and transcripts. If the LTAs are MOUs with no cash and no take-or-pay, the thesis is dead regardless of what 2017 memory or 2000 telecom did. That check should precede assembling four historical episodes.
issues.what_breaks: Analyst time is spent reconstructing prior-cycle conversion histories before establishing whether this company's commitments have any binding quality at all; a doomed idea survives longer than it should.
issues.fix: Front-load the single-name agreement register and tiering as a gate: if this company fails the cash/take-or-pay/RPO-inclusion test, stop before the historical backtest. Use the backtest only to calibrate haircuts once the name clears the first screen.

issues.summary: Haircut percentages (90-95/70/25-35) and the calibration to the 2021-23 semi episode carry heavy weight but rest on a small number of historical episodes with idiosyncratic conversion.
issues.why_it_applies_here: Coverage math and the ≥60%/≥40% thresholds are mechanically driven by these haircuts, yet they are calibrated from a handful of prior cycles that differ in customer concentration and contract structure from this name. A one analyst IC-facing call should not hide sizing sensitivity inside a fixed haircut.
issues.what_breaks: The reverse-DCF horizon comparison and the constructive/negative verdict can flip on plausible haircut choices without the IC seeing that fragility.
issues.fix: Show the coverage conclusion under a haircut band (e.g. Tier 3 at 15% vs 35%) and state where the verdict is robust vs where it hinges on a calibration the analyst cannot defend from this company's own history.

issues.summary: RPO roll-forward solves net bookings as a plug and backs cancellations out of book-to-bill, which is a derived quantity sensitive to FX/M&A and revenue-recognition timing the disclosures may not cleanly separate.
issues.why_it_applies_here: The 'negative implied gross bookings' falsifier depends on the plug being clean. If FX, M&A, or a rev-rec change contaminates the plug, a false negative signal appears — the plan flags negative implied bookings as a kill trigger, so a measurement artifact could kill a live thesis.
issues.what_breaks: The two-quarters-negative kill criterion may fire on an accounting artifact rather than hidden cancellations.
issues.fix: Require the analyst to reconcile any negative implied-bookings quarter against explicitly disclosed FX/M&A/rev-rec items before treating it as a cancellation signal; hand-check one full roll-forward quarter end to end for the IC.

response.overall: A genuinely strong plan, well matched to a concentrated fundamental shop: it is executable by one analyst on Bloomberg/filings, fully inspectable and IC-defensible, appropriately Type-I conservative, and it states a clear variant view (LTA-to-RPO gap, enforceability residue) with real falsifiers and adversarial engagement of the other side. The main improvements are ordering — put the single-name binding-quality screen ahead of the multi-episode backtest so a doomed idea dies in days — and showing the IC how sensitive the verdict is to the calibrated haircuts rather than presenting them as fixed.

issue_buckets.why: Not in gold. A concrete, plan-specific sequencing point: the four-episode backtest is the heaviest item while the Tier 1/2 attribute read on this company's own 8-Ks, commitments footnote and transcripts is a days-long kill. Fits the five-person, one-analyst constraint and a desk would take it seriously.

Same concern as blocking#3 (haircuts calibrated off the 2021-23 semi episode, thin and possibly wrong-industry base) and overlapping secondary#2 (the 90-95/70/25-35 haircuts and the 60%/40% thresholds are asserted rather than derived).

Not in gold and not a recited canonical. response.plan_implied_asker: a systematic cross-industry research shop with database and legal-data infrastructure
response.what_would_falsify: Episodes where contracted price stayed materially above spot for 8+ quarters post-normalization absent a hard qualification moat; and for the live HBM case, pre-registered checks on contract-liability direction, RPO growth, customs shipments, and customer obligation tables.

issues.summary: The plan answers a general cross-industry question about LTA durability rather than the specific single-name call in front of the committee.
issues.why_it_applies_here: The question is whether THIS company's guided shortage portends durable revenue. The plan builds a 20-30 episode cross-industry base-rate framework — a generalizable study — but never names the company, its end market, its qualification lag, or its customers. The deliverable a concentrated committee needs is a verdict on one business, informed by the base rate, not the base rate itself.
issues.what_breaks: The final output ('probability-weighted haircut') is a generic feature-conditional base rate. Step 5's capacity ledger and step 6's breach arithmetic are never applied to the actual name, so the committee cannot act on it.
issues.fix: State the company and its end market up front, classify it on the qualification-lag axis in week one using existing knowledge, and scope the historical work to the 3-5 analogous episodes that share its switching-cost regime. The single most decision-relevant question — is this a moat market or a fungible one — is answerable in days.

issues.summary: The kill test is buried behind building the entire framework; the cheap decisive check comes last.
issues.why_it_applies_here: The plan's own thesis says the outcome is determined by ONE variable: whether in-term requalification is possible. For the specific company, that is largely knowable from product type and industry knowledge before any contract coding or capacity ledger. Yet the plan runs 20-30 episode coding, a per-market capacity ledger, and breach arithmetic before the answer emerges.
issues.what_breaks: An analyst spends weeks coding polysilicon litigation and container rates when the company's classification (fungible vs. moated) could have settled 80% of the question in the first week and either killed or confirmed the durability thesis immediately.
issues.fix: Front-load: classify the target's qualification lag and switching cost first. If clearly fungible, the durability thesis is dead and the higher multiple is unjustified — stop. Only build the full episode library if the case is genuinely marginal.

issues.summary: Scope and data stack are far beyond what one analyst on Bloomberg/Excel/filings can execute or the firm can operate.
issues.why_it_applies_here: The firm has no engineers, no database, no data scientists, and cannot operate infrastructure. The plan requires PACER/Chancery/ICC/SIAC legal scraping, Panjiva/ImportGenius customs data, TrendForce/Fastmarkets/UxC/Argus/Drewry price feeds, a SEMI fab database, and a per-market capacity ledger across ten commodity complexes — a multi-analyst, multi-license, multi-quarter build.
issues.what_breaks: The single analyst cannot complete this; it either stalls or gets executed superficially, and the committee gets a half-built framework rather than an inspectable single-name call.
issues.fix: Cut to the target's own market: the company's and its top customers' 10-K obligation tables, RPO/contract-liability trend, one relevant price series, and 3-4 directly analogous episodes. That is executable by one analyst and defensible.

issues.summary: The output is presented as a 'probability-weighted haircut' but nothing in the plan produces a magnitude for the actual position.
issues.why_it_applies_here: A haircut number implies a quantified revenue/multiple adjustment for the specific name, but the plan never models the company's LTA book size, its share of revenue, or the multiple the market is currently paying for duration. The base rate is cross-industry ordinal scoring, not a P&L input.
issues.what_breaks: A committee sizing off a 'probability-weighted haircut' would be anchoring on a number the analysis did not actually derive for this company.
issues.fix: Frame the deliverable as: which regime the company sits in, what the analogous episodes did to contracted price post-normalization, and what disclosure would confirm/deny durability — leaving sizing to the committee, or explicitly stating what data would let you size it.

response.overall: The economic reasoning is genuinely good — the switching-cost/requalification axis is a real variant view against a market pricing the LTA book as a duration floor, and the falsifier and negative controls (aerospace holds, containers break) are well-constructed. But the plan is written for a systematic shop with legal and customs infrastructure and answers a generalizable cross-industry question, when the firm is a five-person fundamental shop that needs a defensible call on one name. Cut it to the target's own market, front-load the qualification-lag classification (which likely settles the question in a week), and deliver a single-name verdict rather than a base-rate library.

issue_buckets.why: Not in gold, but a legitimate and plan-specific objection: the seed is a single-name call and the plan's deliverable is a cross-industry conditional base rate that never instantiates the named company's qualification lag, customer set, or LTA book. Steps 5 and 6 are indeed specified per-market rather than for the actual position. A concentrated committee would push on this.

Earned from the plan's own logic: the plan asserts switching cost / in-term requalification feasibility is the single determining variable, which for one named company is largely knowable from product type in days. Putting the 20-30 episode coding, capacity ledger, and breach arithmetic ahead of that classification is a real sequencing critique, not a canned one.
Same concern as gold blocking#1 — the data/vendor stack and overall scope exceed what one analyst on Bloomberg/Excel/filings at a five-person shop can execute or the firm can operate.

Specific to this plan's stated output: the plan promises a 'probability-weighted haircut' while its measurement is ordinal outcome scoring and ranked (not regressed) conditional base rates, with no modeling of the name's LTA share of revenue or the duration premium in the multiple. The gap between the ordinal machinery and a quantified haircut is a fair, non-generic point.

response.plan_implied_asker: a concentrated fundamental long-only shop sizing a single-name margin risk from filings and Excel
response.what_would_falsify: If Step 1 sizing shows the licence is a small share of opex and Step 5's inverted required-uplift to breach the guided margin floor lands far above Step 3's observed vendor uplift distribution, the near-term margin risk is immaterial and the defensive-tone concern is abandoned; back-test failing to reproduce the prior renewal's realized move within error bars also invalidates the model.

issues.summary: Vendor negotiated-pricing anchor relies on GSA/Crown Commercial/state schedules that may not reflect this customer's actual discount tier.
issues.why_it_applies_here: Enterprise licence pricing is heavily bespoke; public schedule pricing can be off by a large multiple from what a given customer pays, and the bottom-up spend estimate hinges on the discount-tier haircut, which is the least observable input.
issues.what_breaks: Step 1 bottom-up spend and therefore the entire sensitivity table scale off an anchor that may be systematically wrong; the ~20% top-down/bottom-up reconciliation could mask this because both use the same weak assumption.
issues.fix: Prioritize the top-down purchase-obligations reconciliation as the primary spend anchor and treat bottom-up as a directional cross-check only; flag the discount-tier haircut explicitly as the widest uncertainty band in the IC deliverable.

issues.summary: Comparable-customer uplift distribution (Step 3) may be thin or unobservable for a specific vendor-customer pair.
issues.why_it_applies_here: Finding 5-10 similar customers with disclosed renewal uplifts in 24 months is often not achievable from public sources; the plan already flags survivorship (unpublicized bad deals) but then leans on this distribution to calibrate the central call.
issues.what_breaks: If the comparable set is small or biased toward disclosed favorable renewals, the vendor-behavior input is weakly grounded and the 'forces a call over 75bps' threshold rests on it.
issues.fix: State a minimum comparable-N and pre-commit that if it cannot be met, the conclusion is expressed as a bounded scenario range rather than a point likelihood; the plan's 75th-percentile-as-median adjustment partly handles this but should be made the default when N is low.

response.overall: A well-constructed, appropriately scoped single-name plan that correctly refuses to weight negotiation tone and substitutes a sizeable, filings-based margin-at-stake question executable by one analyst in Excel and fully inspectable by a skeptical IC. It front-loads the kill (size the spend, invert to the required uplift), states real falsifiers, back-tests against the prior renewal, and engages the other side. The only real soft spots are the observability of enterprise discount tiers and the comparable-uplift distribution, both secondary and already partly anticipated.

issue_buckets.why: Not in gold, but a specific, earned critique of Step 1: the bottom-up spend build anchors on GSA/Crown Commercial/state schedule list pricing plus an unobservable discount-tier haircut, and the +/-20% top-down/bottom-up reconciliation can be spuriously satisfied since both legs lean on the same weak anchor. This bites on this plan's named sources rather than being a generic data-quality complaint, and a desk would take it seriously since the whole sensitivity table scales off that number.

Same concern as gold blocking#3 — the comparable-customer uplift distribution underpinning Step 3's likelihood weighting is largely unobservable/biased from public sources, undermining the central-case call and the 75bps trigger.

response.plan_implied_asker: a quant/systematic equity shop with NLP infrastructure and a data-science team
